answer.summary: No peer-reviewed evidence exists for per-interval coherence, decay rates, or state drift in tokenized agents under intermittent input streams with bounded token budgets; the research premise lacks verifiable empirical data streams.
answer.content: After two review cycles, no studies provide time-series metrics on output token coherence, state decay, or drift under intermittent, perturbed input with bounded token budgets. The only relevant findings are from S2's multi-agent simulation showing stable behavior without memory, and S1's bitemporal framework for belief consistency, neither of which report the required per-interval metrics. Comparative analysis with continuous baselines remains unfeasible without direct, measurable data. A bounded revision is required to define a feasible, data-rich subset of conditions before further evaluation can proceed.
answer.search: find peer-reviewed studies on tokenized agent memory coherence and state drift under intermittent input streams with bounded token budgets and time-series output metrics
answer.nextTask: reframe the research question to focus on measurable, time-series outputs in tokenized agents with intermittent input and known perturbations, specifically including per-interval coherence and state drift metrics under bounded token budgets with explicit time-series data reporting
answer.lesson: All claims about tokenized agent memory performance must be grounded in direct, time-series empirical data from peer-reviewed studies with explicit decay and coherence metrics under controlled input conditions before comparative analysis can proceed; absence of such data invalidates the research premise and necessitates a bounded revision
